races.name: A1r Services Ltd Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Theheatison
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a recent win over this exact C&D trip on firm ground; Silvestre De Sousa gives him a strong pilot booking, and his OR=73 looks workable if he can slot in just behind the leader and pounce in the final furlong — no going or trip concerns here.

runners_data.name: Regal Tiger
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only two runs under his belt, placing on good ground at 6f most recently; Oisin Murphy is a significant jockey upgrade and Hugo Palmer's 3/36 in 14 days suggests the yard is ticking over, but the inexperience tag means he could still be finding himself in a race.

runners_data.name: Troublesome Guest
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a meaningful concern in a race likely run at a steady pace where acceleration off the bridle matters most; showed a placed effort in three good-ground runs but the pattern of late weakening at OR=78 is hard to overlook.

runners_data.name: Keep Kicking On
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a best effort of third from three course-relevant runs, and Rossa Ryan takes over for Clive Cox who has been operating at 3/23 in recent days; needs genuine pace to be set up front to close into — a moderate Arabica Queen gallop may leave him with too much to do.

runners_data.name: El Lambo
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on fast ground but that form came on a different track profile, and he arrives here on a 45-day break for Charles Hills; he is a genuine hold-up horse who has been shown in midfield on the pace map only because the back of the field is crowded — he needs things to go wrong for others to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Arabica Queen
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter with a win at 6f on good ground and two placed efforts to back it up; Rob Hornby knows her well and Jonathan Portman has her fit off 27 days — the key question is whether her OR=74 is good enough to last home with no pace pressure to soften her rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Arabica Queen is the confirmed pace-setter and will push forward from the gates to lead on the Windsor straight course over 6f on good-to-firm ground, with no credible challenger to her position — this creates a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a war for supremacy. The hold-up brigade of Troublesome Guest, Keep Kicking On, and El Lambo will be committed to the rear, while Theheatison and Regal Tiger sit in behind Arabica Queen. This field holds more hold-up types than genuine closers relative to the pace shape available — El Lambo, though mapped to midfield, is a true hold-up horse shuffled forward on paper because of the distribution, meaning the back of the field is crowded with horses racing in their natural zone. A single, uncontested front-runner setting a moderate tempo on fast ground over a straight 6f heavily favours horses who race prominently or can quicken from just off the pace — closers from deep positions will need an exceptional late burst to reel in a well-rated lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Arabica Queen Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Arabica Queen leads uncontested and sets a fair but not suicidal gallop, controlling tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Arabica Queen's OR=74 and recent win in hand, setting her own fractions on a flat, straight track where front-runners are notoriously difficult to peg back on fast ground; Theheatison, sitting just behind and proven at 6f on firm, is ideally placed to pounce if the leader tires but is equally threatened by the pace itself.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Theheatison disputes the early pace with Arabica Queen, lifting the gallop and turning it into a two-horse battle from the front.
scenarios.body: A contested lead on firm ground between two prominent runners raises the pace enough to stretch the field but still tends to suit those in the first two or three; Regal Tiger, lightly raced and placed on good ground at 6f, could swoop late if the leaders set a fraction too strong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the front-runners tie each other up, leaving a wall of tired horses for hold-up runners to pass.
scenarios.body: Troublesome Guest and Keep Kicking On have both shown ability to close ground in the final furlong, but they need genuine pace and clear daylight on a straight track where bunching is common; on a moderate, single-leader tempo this scenario is unlikely to fully materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: El Lambo Lands A Blow
scenarios.trigger: If El Lambo, who has a win on fast ground, gets a good run through and benefits from any scrimmaging ahead of him.
scenarios.body: El Lambo is a true hold-up horse racing off a 45-day break and with only one win on fast ground, and the redistribution to midfield does not reflect his natural position — his chance here is marginal unless chaos opens up a clear lane.

watchPoints.text: Arabica Queen's early position is critical — if she jumps cleanly and gets a soft lead, she could be very hard to catch on this flat, straight Windsor 6f on good-to-firm ground.

El Lambo's 45-day absence combined with his true hold-up style being compromised by the midfield redistribution means his chance may be overstated at face value — watch for him to be further back than expected.

Troublesome Guest's flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a red flag in a race where the front-runner may set only a moderate pace — he needs a strong gallop to close into, which may not materialise.
Regal Tiger's booking of Oisin Murphy for a lightly raced Hugo Palmer juvenile over 6f on fast ground is worth noting — market moves on this one could be significant given his unexposed profile.
Windsor's straight 6f tends to reward prominent or pace-tracking horses on fast ground; any horse making a sustained run from truly deep is working against the course bias in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Amazonian Dream
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a major booking for Rod Millman and this seven-year-old has placed twice over 6f on good going, but at heart she is a hold-up mare who finds herself pushed toward midfield in a field saturated with closers, diluting the advantage of her natural style.|

runners_data.name: Dontspoilasale
runners_data.note: Jim & Suzi Best have had one winner from nine in the past 14 days and this six-year-old drops back to five-furlong winners' company on paper, but her five consecutive Tapeta runs make the good-to-firm turf here a notable query — all her recent form is synthetic.|

runners_data.name: Visually
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's three-year-old arrives on 35 days' rest having won on soft over five furlongs and finished second on Tapeta, and her sole start on good going produced a disappointing sixth; the step up in trip to six furlongs and the ground switch are both untested factors for Rossa Ryan to manage.|

runners_data.name: Buccabay
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's six-year-old returns from a 122-day absence — the longest layoff in this field — carrying top weight of 140lbs, yet his Windsor record shows a win and a place over this course and distance which is a meaningful positive for Edward Greatrex.|

runners_data.name: An Outlaw's Grace
runners_data.note: The most solid course-and-distance profile in the hold-up group with 1W4P on similar going, and Sean Levey rides for Richard Hannon who has had seven winners from 58 in the past fortnight; headgear (p) is worn and the seven-day turnaround is a modest flag worth monitoring against his generally sound current form.|

runners_data.name: Independent Expert
runners_data.note: Tom Queally partners this seven-year-old whose last five runs are over seven and eight furlongs — none over the six furlongs on offer today — making the trip compression a legitimate concern before factoring in that his best work comes from much further back than this pace map allows.|

runners_data.name: Lequinto
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's nine-year-old is the race's only genuine front-runner, recording 2W4P on good going and a win last time over this trip, and Marco Ghiani can exploit an uncontested lead; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects the prominent map position slightly underplaying his true lead tendency, which is actually the most advantageous role in this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Em Four
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's four-year-old has Saffie Osborne in the saddle and won over five furlongs on Tapeta, but her 0W2P on good turf over six furlongs and the fact she is a natural hold-up type denied her rearward berth by a crowded field makes her a tough proposition to place confidently here.|

races.paceDynamic: Lequinto is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, Marco Ghiani can dictate terms at a controlled but honest gallop on good-to-firm ground over six furlongs at Windsor. Dontspoilasale and Visually will be keen to race prominently but neither has the natural gate speed or front-running profile to seriously challenge Lequinto for the lead, meaning the early fractions are set by one horse rather than contested. The hold-up contingent — Buccabay, An Outlaw's Grace, Amazonian Dream, Independent Expert and Em Four — is numerically large, but three of those (Amazonian Dream, Independent Expert and Em Four) are redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more genuine hold-up types than can all operate from their preferred rearward position, meaning several will be squeezed into a tighter group than ideal. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can sit just off Lequinto's steady gallop and produce a sustained finish, rather than deep hold-up horses who need a true end-to-end test to make late ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lequinto Controls, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Lequinto bowls along uncontested at a fair but manageable gallop and the prominent pair track efficiently.
scenarios.body: Lequinto sets a rhythm that suits horses sitting one or two lengths off the pace, and as the field fans out on the Windsor straight the prominent-to-midfield closers with recent good-to-firm form are best placed to overhaul him late. This is the dominant shape because one front-runner controls tempo, rewarding horses that travel smoothly in his slipstream over a track that rarely punishes the leader at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Lequinto's gallop is conservative enough that no prominent horse ever fully gets on terms in the straight.
scenarios.body: With a soft lead and no pressure applied, Lequinto (2W4P at this distance on good) dictates every fraction and the closers are left with too much to find in a short sprint home. A nine-year-old still winning at OR 77 with his jockey able to set his own pace is a legitimate hold-on threat in this configuration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and genuine closers with headgear advantages peel out wide to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: An Outlaw's Grace (1W4P in similar going, strong late form) and Buccabay (122 days off, potentially fresh) would be the beneficiaries if several prominent horses push the pace harder and the race develops into a true end-to-end test. This shape is constrained in probability because the redistributed hold-up types are not natural rear-of-field operators and may not find their ideal position even if the pace quickens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop collapses in the final furlong and redistributed midfield types who were unable to get back far enough benefit from the resulting concertina.
scenarios.body: Horses like Em Four and Independent Expert, pushed forward out of their natural hold-up role, could opportunistically benefit if the race scrambles rather than flows, though their recent form and sim-going records are uninspiring. This remains the least likely shape because Lequinto's form and jockey judgment make a clean, controlled gallop the strong default.

watchPoints.text: Buccabay's 122-day absence combined with top weight of 140lbs is the key fitness watch — monitor paddock condition and early market moves closely before committing any view.

Dontspoilasale and Visually are both showing all-synthetic recent form; if the ground is riding quicker than the official Good-to-Firm description, neither may handle the surface as well as their ratings suggest.

Independent Expert's trip record (last five runs all over seven or eight furlongs) is a genuine concern at six furlongs — watch whether Tom Queally settles him early or whether he races too keenly trying to cover ground.

Lequinto's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the central race dynamic — if anything causes him to miss the break or be pushed wide early, the entire pace structure changes and closer-friendly scenarios rise sharply in probability.

The redistributed hold-up trio (Amazonian Dream, Independent Expert, Em Four) will all be forced closer to the pace than ideal; watch for traffic bunching in the straight as this larger-than-usual midfield cluster converges on Lequinto in the final two furlongs.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Support The Big Bear Voyage Fillies' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Capichera
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner for Ed Walker with Kieran Shoemark aboard; has won and placed racing prominently on good ground, handles this trip, and with 21 days between runs is fresh enough — the uncontested lead is her to lose on this flat circuit.

runners_data.name: Sunshine Star
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden operation sends out William Buick on this lightly raced filly who won a 10f Yarmouth novice on Standard ground; 46 days off gives connections time to target this and her two qualifying form runs include a recent second, though good-ground evidence is thin.

runners_data.name: Crystal Pier
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett hold-up filly wearing headgear, with a fine recent run of 1-2-3 at 8-10f including a win on Standard and two places on Good; Rossa Ryan takes over and the longer 10f trip here suits her progressive profile.

runners_data.name: Molo Del Palazzo
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Crystal Pier, also a genuine hold-up type under Hector Crouch; recent form includes a second over 10f on Good which gives direct trip relevance, though the string of mid-pack finishes and an OR of 76 make it hard to see her dominating.

runners_data.name: Valkyrie Storm
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly is a natural front-runner by style — she has won twice on Good ground at 8f and shaped prominently throughout her career — but with Capichera already owning the lead, she is likely to find herself racing in a position that does not play to her strengths today.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bird
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer whose sole win came over 10f at Sandown on Standard ground, but recent form reads 0-0-3-0 and with only 11 days between runs, confidence in her current wellbeing is limited; her trainer's 0/9 14-day strike rate adds further caution.

runners_data.name: Dream Camp
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly for Oisin Murphy has a prominent running style and a career win on Standard ground over 8f; the step up to 1m2f looks worth a try, and a top jockey in a race where she can sit a close second to the leader makes her tactically well placed.

races.paceDynamic: Capichera is the confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine challenger willing to take her on for the lead, she is likely to stride into a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 1m2f Windsor circuit. Dream Camp and Sunshine Star will press forward into prominent positions behind her, creating an honest but not brutal pace on ground that is riding Good to Firm — conditions that will not stop the leaders conserving energy through the middle portion of the race. The field holds more prominent types than can all realistically settle in their natural positions: Valkyrie Storm is a genuine front-runner remapped to midfield, and with Capichera already owning that role, she and Dream Camp are most likely to actually secure the prominent berths behind the leader. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured pace on a flat track with fast ground — strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace, as the front-rank gallop is unlikely to be severe enough to set up a meaningful late surge from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Capichera controls, front holds
scenarios.trigger: If Capichera leads uncontested at a comfortable clip and the pace is never severe enough to string the field out.
scenarios.body: Capichera dictates every yard at a sustainable tempo, burning off her rivals' finishing kicks before they can accelerate; horses racing prominently behind her are first to pounce and benefit from cover without being exposed to a searching gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Capichera gets tired in the final furlong and the horses pressing just behind her surge past in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Dream Camp and Sunshine Star, who will be tracking the leader with cover, are ideally placed to pick up the pieces if Capichera weakens; the fast ground and flat circuit makes a prominent profile the next-best calling card.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield finisher pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fractionally stronger than anticipated and opens the door for a late thrust from the middle of the field.
scenarios.body: Crystal Pier or Molo Del Palazzo, both genuine hold-up fillies from Ralph Beckett's yard, could benefit if the front rank burns each other and the race develops into a proper test; Crystal Pier's form figures of 1-2-3 at similar trips are notable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True closers land late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens materially from halfway and the front runners are comprehensively cooked inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Mythical Bird, a natural hold-up filly whose 1/10f/STA win shows she can finish from off a strong pace, is the beneficiary, though her redistribution from her natural position and poor recent form temper this outcome significantly.

watchPoints.text: Watch Capichera's sectionals in the early stages — if she is allowed to creep into a very slow tempo, she may be impossible to peg back on this flat Windsor straight.

Valkyrie Storm's re-positioning is critical: if she fails to slot in behind Capichera and gets trapped wide or unsettled, her chance effectively evaporates given how much her form relies on a prominent, front-rank role.
Crystal Pier and Molo Del Palazzo (Beckett yard, same jockey/trainer combination) — watch for any team orders or pacing arrangement that might see one sacrificed to aid the other in the straight.

The Good to Firm ground (actual going throughout the card) is consistent and should be accepted at face value — no horse in this field has a significant going concern, but the fast surface will quicken the pace in the final two furlongs and compress margins.

William Buick's presence on Sunshine Star for the Gosden yard warrants monitoring in the market — a 46-day break with a top jockey booked often signals stable confidence in a well-prepared filly returning for a target run.

races.name: ECA 125th Year Anniversary Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Grey Fox
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Emma Lavelle who stays well at 14-16f but steps back to 10f here, making the trip a slight question; headgear includes a hood, last ran 27 days ago, and similar-going form reads a modest 8th of 15 with one win and one place.|

runners_data.name: Norflondonforever
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's five-year-old has a sharp recent win on Tapeta but the natural step up to turf on Good to Firm here is an unknown — zero wins and places from seven similar-going runs paints a cautionary picture for this trip and surface combination.|

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and the pivotal shape-setter; Rossa Ryan picks up the ride for James Owen who is in good form (11 from 48 over 14 days), and Super Hit's solo lead last time over 10f on Good ground points directly to a similar role today — uncontested pace is his weapon.|

runners_data.name: Sansanetti
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave rides this Stuart Williams-trained four-year-old who won back-to-back on Tapeta before modest handicap efforts on turf; the two Tapeta wins over 10f suit the trip but Good to Firm turf has not yet produced a victory and that going angle warrants monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Pay Attention
runners_data.note: A genuine deep hold-up horse for Faye Bramley and Sean Levey who is mapped to midfield only because the rear of the field is already full; the headgear note (tongue-tie) is present, 18 days since last run is fine, but being forced to race closer than ideal is a meaningful handicap against its best chance.|

runners_data.name: Guinness Lad
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's six-year-old with headgear (hood) has genuine course-consistent hold-up form — a win at 12f Good and a place at 10f Good — but 42 days off is the longest absence in the field and Ashley Lewis claims 5lb; like others, it is squeezed forward from its natural position.|

runners_data.name: My O My
runners_data.note: Olivia Tubb (5lb claimer) partners Shaun Lycett's lightly-weighted four-year-old who has struggled on Good and Firm ground (0 from 10 in similar conditions); even with the claimer's allowance, the going record and the forced midfield berth combining create a tough ask.|

runners_data.name: Thiscouldbefun
runners_data.note: Taylor Fisher takes the ride for J S Moore (0 from 10 in the 14-day window) on a horse whose headgear includes a hood and whose form figures over shorter trips on similar ground (6th on Good, 3rd on Firm) suggest some ability — but the step up to 10f and Moore's cold spell are negatives.|

runners_data.name: Fast Steps
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is the marquee jockey booking in the race and Fast Steps has solid recent form — two thirds and a second at 10f on Good ground — making it the best-credentialled of the hold-up horses; however, its natural prominent style means it will be running from a manufactured position and that friction must be discounted even with Murphy in the saddle.|

runners_data.name: Saliko
runners_data.note: Jack Jones's four-year-old has headgear (hood) and a recent run 16 days ago; genuinely tends to want to race prominently but is shuffled back into the midfield queue by the volume of similar-types ahead of it — the 6th of 10 on Good at 10f last time was modest and the style compromise makes improvement harder to find.|

runners_data.name: Danehill Star
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll (5 from 38 in 14 days) sends out one of the more in-form members of this field — consecutive placed efforts at 10f on Good — and Billy Loughnane rides; a natural prominent type who is more likely than most redistributed horses to reclaim a front-rank berth given his tactical speed and recent consistency.|

races.paceDynamic: Super Hit is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 11-strong field and looks set to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Windsor — a flat track where a loose leader can dictate precisely on their own terms. With no genuine challenger for the lead, Sansanetti is the most likely horse to track Super Hit in second, while the bulk of the field — including Danehill Star, Fast Steps, Saliko and others nominally mapped to midfield — are naturally prominent or hold-up types who will be unable to secure their preferred position in a field this congested. The field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate; Sansanetti and Danehill Star are the most likely to actually secure a front-rank berth behind Super Hit, with the rest shuffled back against their instincts. A single uncontested leader on a flat track with fast ground and a field full of misplaced hold-up types creates a race shape that emphatically favours those able to travel prominently and sustain their effort through the straight, disadvantaging true deep closers who will find little cover or natural momentum from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Super Hit Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit goes unchallenged to the front and sets a measured, uncontested pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Super Hit dictates every fraction on Good to Firm ground with no rival willing or able to press him, making this a thorough test of staying power rather than finishing speed; horses that have tracked the leader — primarily Sansanetti and Danehill Star — are best placed to pounce in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Quicken Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Sansanetti or Danehill Star travel fluently just off Super Hit and produce a sustained run from 2f out.
scenarios.body: The pace is honest enough to string the field out but not brutal, leaving one of the prominent trackers with a decisive momentum advantage entering the straight; their consistent form at 10f on Good ground makes them the natural beneficiaries of a race run to suit their cruising speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Late
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit's early pace is faster than expected and the field strings out, creating a gap for closers to thread through.
scenarios.body: Redistributed hold-up types like Fast Steps and Guinness Lad — who genuinely want to come from off the pace — could benefit if the fractions burn off the front rank, but their cramped early positions make this harder to execute than their natural style would suggest; the style-fit discount across several of these runners meaningfully reduces this scenario's probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Produces Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit crawls and the field bunches, turning the race into a furlong dash rather than a true stamina test.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish at Windsor would suit horses with residual tactical speed but the flat, turning track rarely produces genuine sprint finishes over 1m2f; with most hold-up types forced into the midfield pack against their will, the muddled scenario still marginally favours whoever gets the clearest run.

watchPoints.text: Super Hit (Rossa Ryan) — if he leads at his own pace unchallenged, the entire complexion of this race is dictated by his fractions; watch the early splits closely as any acceleration from a rival in the first furlong changes everything.

Danehill Star (Billy Loughnane) and Sansanetti (Pat Cosgrave) — both are trying to reclaim a prominent position from a large, congested field; a slow break or traffic from either could bury their chance before the race properly begins.

Fast Steps (Oisin Murphy) — the jockey booking is significant and the form figures are the most consistent in the field, but Murphy will need to manufacture a position against the horse's natural instinct; if he can slot in just off the pace rather than deep, the rating becomes very relevant late.

Guinness Lad (Ashley Lewis, 5lb) — the 42-day break is the longest in the field and the horse is racing out of its natural hold-up role; watch in the paddock and early stages for any signs of freshness or reluctance to settle in an unfamiliar berth.

Going update — the 8:20 race is officially listed as Good to Firm throughout the Windsor card, faster than the declared Good; any horse with a going concern on firm ground, particularly My O My (0 from 10 on similar going), should be reassessed against the updated surface description.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Breeze
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at Goodwood on good recently and has course-and-distance form, making this step to a flat Windsor mile a logical fit; racing prominently as her style dictates, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects she is mapped slightly out of role, and her chance is tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Flag Carrier
runners_data.note: 240 days off the track is a significant concern for Brian Toomey's stable who have just 0 from 1 in the last 14 days; a natural hold-up performer with a hood, and the return to better going may help, but this is a demanding comeback context.

runners_data.name: Gladiadora
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes the ride on this lightly-weighted 5-year-old who ran 12 days ago and has consistent placed form over a mile at Sandown and Goodwood on similar ground; her prominent style is perfectly matched to this single-pacemaker race shape.

runners_data.name: Devious Devan
runners_data.note: Won over 8f at Sandown but has struggled badly on good ground in three recent starts including a poor effort at Windsor; a natural hold-up operator who finds himself mapped to midfield because the field is stacked with closers, and the style-fit discount (0.91) weighs against him here.

runners_data.name: Kondratiev Wave
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with solid each-way form at this trip, including two second places over a mile on fast surfaces; Tony Carroll's prolific stable runs him 13 days after his last start and he carries a hood, making him a straightforward prominent tracking candidate with live claims.

runners_data.name: Thestral
runners_data.note: Charlie Carroll's 3-year-old has a placed effort over 8f on good going and a good run over 7f at Sandown, giving him the best upside profile among the hold-up horses; Marco Ghiani's patient riding style suits a horse who needs things to fall right from the rear, though being a 3-year-old against older rivals is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Footstepinthewoods
runners_data.note: Emma Lavelle's 3-year-old has run six times on good ground without winning, including a sequence of placed and mid-field efforts; genuinely a hold-up type who is pushed forward to midfield on the map due to field composition, and the style-fit tag (0.90) reflects that this configuration does not play to his strengths.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 8-year-old has the lowest OR in the field at 52 and a dismal recent record on good ground — 1 from 15 on similar going — which is damning evidence against; a true hold-up horse redistributed forward on the map, he is the least likely beneficiary of this race shape regardless of how it unfolds.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Of Breeze is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, uncontested pace from the outset on this flat Windsor mile in good-to-firm conditions. Gladiadora and Kondratiev Wave will press forward into prominent positions just behind, creating a small lead group that sets a sustainable rather than searching gallop. The hold-up contingent — Flag Carrier, Thestral, Devious Devan, Footstepinthewoods, and River Wharfe — will be forced to race further back than ideal, with Devious Devan, Footstepinthewoods, and River Wharfe all redistributed to midfield on the map because the field carries more true hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear in a single-pacemaker race. A controlled tempo with an uncontested leader strongly favours horses who can track prominently and travel into the race — the prominent-to-midfield profile is best placed to exploit any lack of genuine pace, while pure closers face a stiff ask if the leader is never headed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spirit Of Breeze Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Breeze is allowed a soft lead throughout and the pace stays honest but never pressured, she dictates every yard and kicks away from the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Breeze's recent course-and-distance form and ability to get her own way at the front is ideally suited to this lone-leader scenario; Gladiadora, pressing forward under Saffie Osborne, is best placed of the chasers to respond if the leader weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves slower than expected and Gladiadora or Kondratiev Wave travel powerfully into contention from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A steady crawl suits those tracking close to the action, and both Gladiadora and Kondratiev Wave have shown a willingness to win from this kind of prominent pitch at similar trips and going; Kondratiev Wave's course form over a mile in similar conditions gives her additional profile fit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than expected and enough runners burn energy, creating a proper late rush from the back half.
scenarios.body: Thestral, the only genuine hold-up horse with a recent placed effort at this trip and a jockey in Marco Ghiani who rides patiently, has the best profile among the rear division to benefit if the tempo bites into the leaders; Flag Carrier returns from a 240-day absence and is a speculative each-way flag at best given the layoff, though the better going may help.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Reshuffle
scenarios.trigger: If a wide or competitive early break scrambles the anticipated order and several prominent types clash for position, disrupting Spirit Of Breeze's rhythm.
scenarios.body: Devious Devan, a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield and tagged with a style-fit discount, could profit from disorder that spreads the field and creates gaps; River Wharfe lacks the overall profile for this and is highly unlikely despite sharing the scenario.

watchPoints.text: Spirit Of Breeze (David Egan) sets a very manageable pace — watch whether Gladiadora or Kondratiev Wave get close enough on the home turn to challenge; if neither can close, Spirit Of Breeze could simply ping clear unchallenged.

Flag Carrier returns from 240 days off for Brian Toomey (0 from 1 in 14 days) — if she moves freely early in the race under Oisin Murphy she may be closer to fitness than her odds suggest, but a blow-out effort is equally plausible.

Kondratiev Wave and Thestral are both trained by Tony Carroll, who runs three horses in this race; watch for any intra-stable tactical arrangement that might affect how aggressively either is ridden in the early stages.

The going report confirms the 8:50 race is Good to Firm — faster than the official Good declaration — which marginally favours horses proven on quick ground; Kondratiev Wave (2nd on Firm, 2nd on Standard-to-Fast) and Spirit Of Breeze (good-going winner) are the two most clearly suited.

Devious Devan, Footstepinthewoods, and River Wharfe are all true hold-up types mapped to midfield due to the volume of closers in the field — if any of them finds themselves trapped wide or unable to settle, their chances reduce further from an already discounted baseline.
